chunks: And I do not say to you that I have the treasures of God, nor do I know the unseen, nor do I say that I am an angel, nor do I say to those whom your eyes disdain that God will not bestow good upon them; God is knowing of what is in their souls; if I did, I would surely be among the unjust.

key_terms.إِنِّي إِذًا لَمِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ: If I did, I would surely be among the unjust

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the Prophet's knowledge of the unseen and divine treasures?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to affirm the Prophet's human nature and distinctness from angels, while also serving as a basis for the concept of *al-ghayb* (the unseen) being granted to prophets and Imams by divine permission rather than inherent divinity. It addresses the skepticism of early followers who doubted the Prophet's impartiality, reinforcing that divine favor is rooted in God's knowledge of inner states, not human perception. This underscores the theological principle that prophets are servants of God, not possessors of independent divine attributes.
